newsitem.title: USA: Perceptron to buy two firms.
newsitem.headline: Perceptron to buy two firms.

text.p: Perceptron Inc said Tuesday it had signed letters of intent to acquire Trident Systems Inc of Atlanta and Nanoose Systems Corp of Parksville, British Columbia.
The deals are expected to be slightly accretive to earnings in 1997, Perceptron said.
The acquisitions will broaden Perceptron's new forest products businesses, it said.
Trident and Nanoose will operate as subsidiaries of Perceptron, and their current management teams will continue to provide leadership, it said.

Perceptron said it expects the acquisitions will account for at least 10 percent of its total revenues. Perceptron, which makes measurement and guidance systems for industry, had revenues of $50 million in 1996.

The acquisitions are structured to be accounted for as poolings of interests. Terms will be disclosed after closing, which is subject to a number of factors including definitive documents and completion of satisfactory due diligence, Perceptron said.

It said it entered into a marketing and distribution agreement with Trident in 1995, making Trident the primary integrator of Perceptron sensors for systems to be sold to the forest products marketplace.
Optimization software written by Nanoose has been a key element of the integrated systems Trident develops and sells, Perceptron said.

Trident is full service systems integrator for the solid woods sector of the forest products industry. Nanoose is a software design and engineering company specializing in industrial scanning and optimization systems.

Perceptron said it estimates the North American market for optimization systems at more than $60 million. Additional markets include Australia and New Zealand, where systems have already been sold. South America and Europe also represent significant potential marketplaces, it said.
